title: How to Track SwipePages Forms in GTM, From a Live Landing Page
intro:
This client's main site runs on one platform, and the paid traffic lands on a SwipePages page on its own subdomain. So there are two sources of leads, and they need to be reported separately.

Earlier this week, I submitted a clearly labelled test lead on that landing page with GTM Preview open. The event fired once, and the contact details came through ready for Enhanced Conversions.

Here's how that setup works, from the real container with the names removed.
tldr: This free script counts a lead when SwipePages confirms the form went through. If your landing page is on its own subdomain, you can report its leads separately from your main site, so you can see which one is producing.
sections: Why SwipePages needs its own signal

SwipePages marks a successful submission with a class on the form, so that's what the listener watches:

What happensSignalResult
SwipePages accepts the leadamp-form-submit-success classswipe_form_success, method confirmation_class
Redirect to a same-domain thank-you pageMatched to recent stored form dataswipe_form_success
Submission erroramp-form-submit-error classswipe_form_failed
Tatsu form or terms warning showsVisible warning after interactionswipe_form_failed

SwipePages' own guide uses GTM's Form Submission trigger with a CSS class you add to each form. It avoids a thank-you page and is quick to set up, but it doesn't cover failed submissions or contact data. If you only need a count, try that first. I needed contact data for Enhanced Conversions, and no per-form setup.

1. Download the GTM tag, or get it from GitHub.
  2. Paste it into a new Custom HTML tag, triggered on All Pages.
  3. Check that your GTM container is actually on the landing page, since it's a separate build from your main site.

The tag setup is the same as the Gravity Forms walkthrough. If your main site uses a different form tool, use the universal listener walkthrough instead, as this account does.
Step 2: Split the trigger by hostname

Create a Custom Event trigger on swipe_form_success. If the landing page lives on its own subdomain, set Some Custom Events and add a Page Hostname condition.

[[img:swipe-trigger|Landing page leads only, feeding Google Ads and Meta.]]

With one trigger per hostname, each lead source gets its own conversion action, and you can see which one is producing.
Step 3: Connect Google Ads, Meta and GA4

Attach your tags to that trigger. This account adds form_position and form_id to the Google Ads tag, so a page with two forms can be told apart.

[[img:swipe-gads-tag|The landing page conversion.]]

Send form details to GA4, and map ec_email and ec_phone in a User-Provided Data variable for Enhanced Conversions.

Want these in reports? GA4 won't show them until you register each one as a custom dimension. Here's how.

1. In Preview, load the landing page and expect ec_tracker_initialized.
  2. Submit a labelled test lead. Expect one swipe_form_success, with ec_detection_method of confirmation_class.
  3. Open the event and check the ec_* values, including that the phone variable reads ec_phone.
  4. Confirm the main site's conversion didn't fire too.

Then remove old click or thank-you conversions for this page.

• The labelled test lead ran on an earlier build, on a live landing page, with contact data coming through.
  • For v3.3.0, I loaded the build on that same page, filled in the real form and triggered the success class without sending a lead. It returned a normalised email and phone, first and last name, and the ZIP.
  • Leaving a required field empty on that page only triggered the browser's own validation. No failure event fired, and no success either. Don't rely on swipe_form_failed to count those.
  • A redirect to a different domain can't use the stored data.

Can I track SwipePages conversions without a thank-you page?

Yes. The listener fires when SwipePages adds its success class to the form, so no redirect is needed.

How do I keep landing page leads separate in Google Ads?

Add a Page Hostname condition to the trigger, then give each hostname its own conversion action.
